title: Towards Unified Analysis of GPU Consistency
problem: GPU consistency models (Nvidia PTX and Khronos Vulkan) are complex and difficult for developers to interpret, requiring expertise beyond most programmers' reach with insufficient tool support for analyzing program correctness.
motivation: Growing popularity of general-purpose GPU programming demands formal clarity and developer-accessible tools for understanding GPU consistency guarantees.
method: The approach formalizes Nvidia PTX and Khronos Vulkan consistency models—the rules governing how GPUs handle memory operations across parallel threads—and analyzes both to identify which rules they share and which differ between vendors. It then develops tools and frameworks based on this analysis, enabling developers to verify their GPU code will behave correctly under these different consistency rules without requiring deep GPU architecture expertise.
key_novelty: A unified framework for analyzing Nvidia PTX and Khronos Vulkan consistency models together, revealing which memory rules they share and where they diverge.
contributions: Formalization and comparison of GPU consistency models (PTX and Vulkan)
Developer-friendly tools for interpreting GPU consistency guarantees
Analysis framework for verifying GPU program correctness against consistency models
Accessibility improvements for GPU memory model semantics
limitations: Specific limitations and empirical evaluation scope not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: unified GPU consistency analysis and tools
